title: The Busiest Travel Days of the Year and How to Plan for Them
summary: Learn the busiest travel days of the year, when airport crowds tend to peak, and how to plan a more predictable trip.
body_markdown:
Airport crowds ebb and flow throughout the year. Holiday weekends create sharp spikes, while spring break and summer bring longer stretches of high passenger volume. Knowing when airports tend to be busiest can help you prepare for each part of your trip. Here are the peak travel periods to watch and practical ways to plan for them.
‍


> *Editor’s Note: Travel patterns change by year, airport, and destination. Check your flight, airport conditions, and live security wait times before leaving home.*


‍


## **The Busiest Travel Periods at a Glance**


Travel Period When Airports Tend to Be Busiest What to Expect


Spring break March and April, depending on school calendars Several weeks of higher passenger volume rather than one national peak day


Memorial Day The days before and after the holiday weekend The start of the busy summer travel season


Summer travel June through August, especially Fridays and Sundays Sustained high volume, with additional spikes around holiday weekends


Fourth of July The days surrounding July 4, especially the return weekend Some of the year’s highest single-day airport totals


Labor Day The Friday before the holiday and the return weekend A final summer travel surge


Thanksgiving The Tuesday and Wednesday before Thanksgiving and the Sunday after The Sunday return is often one of the busiest days of the year


Christmas and New Year’s The final departure days before Christmas and the return period after the holiday Crowds spread across multiple dates based on the calendar


‍


## **Is There One Busiest Travel Day of the Year?**


There is not one date that is busiest every year. The calendar, school schedules, weather, and the day of the week on which a holiday falls can all shift travel patterns.


The Sunday after Thanksgiving frequently creates one of the largest single-day airport crowds because many travelers return home at the same time. Summer can drive equally large or larger airport volumes across a longer period.


Instead of relying on one annual date to make your plans, the smarter approach is to watch recurring peak periods. For a consistent comparison,[TSA screened](https://www.tsa.gov/travel/passenger-volumes) an average of about 2.47 million travelers per day from January 1 through November 9, 2026. The percentages below compare each period’s busiest day with that daily average.


‍


## **Spring Break Travel**


Spring break is one of the first sustained busy travel periods of the year. Since school calendars vary, the rush is spread across several weeks in March and April rather than concentrated on one weekend.


Across March and April 2026, TSA’s final daily checkpoint totals show 152,795,753 screenings. The busiest day was Sunday, March 22, when TSA screened 2,865,969 travelers, about 16% more than on an average 2026 day.


If you are traveling during spring break, confirm your terminal and checkpoint before leaving home. Families should also review airline rules, baggage limits, and any documents needed for children before arriving at the airport.


‍


## **Summer Travel from Memorial Day Through Labor Day**


Summer brings a long period of high airport volume rather than a single rush. The TSA treats Memorial Day weekend as the start of the summer travel season and Labor Day as the end.


From May 21 through September 7, 2026, TSA’s final daily totals show 286,216,431 screenings, or about 2.6 million per day. The busiest day was Thursday, June 18, with 2,988,204 travelers screened, about 21% more than on an average 2026 day.


### **Memorial Day Weekend**


Memorial Day kicks off the summer surge. In 2026, TSA’s final daily checkpoint totals show 18,431,515 screenings from Thursday, May 21, through Wednesday, May 27. The busiest day was Friday, May 22, with 2,976,209 travelers screened—about 21% more than on an average 2026 day.


### **Fourth of July Travel**


The Fourth of July period regularly produces some of the year’s highest passenger totals. TSA’s final daily checkpoint totals show that 18,301,871 travelers were screened from Tuesday, June 30, through Monday, July 6, 2026.


The peak was Sunday, July 5, when TSA screened 2,914,375 travelers, about 18% more than on an average 2026 day. The exact peak changes with the calendar, so check current forecasts rather than assuming the busiest day will fall before or after the holiday.


### **Labor Day Weekend**


Labor Day creates one final summer rush. The Friday before the holiday is often a major departure day, followed by another increase as travelers return at the end of the weekend.


From Friday, September 4, through Monday, September 7, 2026, TSA’s final daily checkpoint totals show 9,843,653 screenings. Friday was the busiest day, with 2,815,644 travelers screened—about 14% more than on an average 2026 day.


‍


## **Thanksgiving Travel**


Thanksgiving creates one of the sharpest travel spikes of the year. For 2026, CLEAR expects Friday, November 20, to be the busiest pre-Thanksgiving travel day, followed by Wednesday, November 25. Sunday, November 29, is expected to be the season’s busiest travel day as travelers return home.


[Airlines for America](https://www.airlines.org/) (A4A) projects that U.S. airlines will carry nearly 29 million passengers over the Thanksgiving travel period. A4A represents leading U.S. passenger and cargo airlines, so its forecast reflects the schedules and capacity carriers expect to operate. Higher volume can mean fuller flights, busier check-in and bag-drop areas, and fewer open seats for rebooking when disruptions occur.


A4A counts passengers flying on U.S. airlines, while TSA counts checkpoint screenings, so the figures should not be compared directly.


Airport security lines are expected to peak from 5 to 7 a.m. and remain busy until about 6 p.m. local time. If you are flying on Sunday, November 29, check in as soon as your airline allows and confirm your terminal, checkpoint, and gate. Plan for parking or rideshare drop-off, bag check, airport security, and the walk to your gate.


‍


## **Christmas and New Year’s Travel**


Christmas and New Year’s crowds are usually spread across more dates than the Thanksgiving rush. The busiest days depend on where the holidays fall during the week and when schools and offices close.


For 2026, CLEAR expects Friday, December 18, to be the busiest Christmas departure day. Tuesday, December 22, and Wednesday, December 23, are also expected to bring larger crowds than usual. The return rush is expected to peak on Sunday, December 27, with crowds beginning to ease around 5 p.m.


Across the Christmas travel period, airport security lines are expected to be busiest from 5 to 7 a.m., with smaller crowds later in the day. A smaller crowd does not guarantee that a flight will operate on time. Winter weather, aircraft schedules, and conditions at other airports can still affect the trip.


These forecasts are based on prior travel patterns and may change. Check your flight, airport conditions, and live security wait times before leaving home.


‍


## **How to Plan for the Busiest Travel Days**


### **Prepare the Day Before**


Check in for your flight as soon as your airline allows, save your boarding pass, and confirm your departure terminal and gate. Review baggage rules before packing, especially if you are bringing gifts, food, sports equipment, or winter gear.


Charge your phone and portable battery, turn on flight notifications, and keep medication, travel documents, and other essentials in your carry-on. A little preparation can reduce the number of decisions you need to make in a busy terminal.


‍


### **Know When to Leave with the CLEAR App**


Once your trip is booked, download the free[CLEAR App](https://www.clearme.com/clear-mobile-app) to get everything you need, exactly when you need it from home to gate. Sync your flight to know exactly when to leave based on real-time traffic, airport conditions, and your preferred arrival time.


At the airport, use the app to find the CLEAR+ Lane, check live airport security wait times, and pre-order your Starbucks to have it ready and waiting for pickup on the way to your gate.


### **Prepare for Airport Security**


Confirm your terminal and checkpoint before leaving home. Airport construction, airline assignments, and checkpoint hours can change, so review current information on your airport’s website and in the CLEAR App.


CLEAR+ Members can unlock access to over 150 CLEAR+ Lanes at airports nationwide, so they can turn travel days into great days. If you plan to use CLEAR+, check[where to use CLEAR+](https://www.clearme.com/where-to-use-clear) for current availability and hours.


### **Prepare for Delays and Connections**


Turn on airline notifications and review other flights to your destination in case your schedule changes. Keep a charger, medication, and anything you may need during a delay in your carry-on rather than a checked bag.


If you have a connection, check your next gate as soon as you land. On a busy travel day, head toward that gate before stopping for food or shopping, especially if you have a short connection.


‍

‍


## **Prepare for Peak Travel Throughout the Year**


Busy airports are not limited to Thanksgiving and Christmas. Spring break, long summer weekends, and the periods around Memorial Day, Fourth of July, and Labor Day can all bring high passenger volume.


Prepare the day before, know when to leave, and check current airport and flight conditions before heading out. Once your trip is booked, use the free[CLEAR App](https://www.clearme.com/clear-mobile-app) to plan your travel day from home to gate and stay informed along the way.
